Magnesium levulinate is directly linked to Alkaline phosphatase, placental type, which is a target of the Influenza B virus B/Hong Kong/259/2010 hemagglutinin antigen. This viral antigen, in turn, targets Calcium transporting ATPases. This chain of interactions implies that Magnesium levulinate may influence the activity of Calcium transporting ATPases through its effect on Alkaline phosphatase. The evidence suggests a possible regulatory or functional link, though the exact mechanism remains unclear. The relationship is supported by a high confidence score, indicating a strong, though indirect, connection between the two entities.
